key_insight: A quantum convolutional neural network can act as a surrogate model for groundwater heat plume prediction, delivering competitive but not yet class-leading accuracy versus classical neural networks.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a compact quantum workflow for environmental prediction problems where full-resolution simulation outputs are too large for near-term quantum hardware.
method: Reduced high-dimensional simulation outputs to representative target parameters for surrogate training.
Built a QCNN with quantum convolution, quantum pooling, and quantum readout layers.
Used Hamiltonian-inspired feature encoding and tested on statevector, noisy, and real IBM Kyoto hardware with error mitigation.
evidence_signal: Performance was evaluated with mean squared error on training and test sets across ideal simulation, noisy simulation, IBM 127-qubit hardware, and hardware plus error mitigation.
watch_item: The surrogate depends on aggressive output reduction and still trails classical neural networks, so hardware scalability and practical accuracy remain key constraints.
paper_title: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks for Groundwater Heat Plume Prediction: A Surrogate Modeling Approach
